config.reference: average (64 scalp channels; EOG excluded); data shipped with mastoid-average reference
config.method: ridge backward decoder, 64 ch, lags 0-250 ms, lambda 0.1 x mean eigenvalue, 64 Hz, 0.5-8 Hz (demean + linear detrend per trial before resampling), leave-one-trial-out within the decoder set (pooled 30 trials, events 22, quiet 8); nulls per held-out trial: 50 circular shifts (>= 5 s) and the 29 other lessons' envelopes (np.resize); fixed-decoder lag sweep and refit lag sweep +-1 s in 1-sample (15.6 ms) steps; parabolic peak, subject-bootstrap CI
config.stimulus: authors' 100 Hz speech envelope (speech only; distractor sounds not in it), resampled to 64 Hz, cut with the EEG to the shorter length
config.pass_criterion: population p_circ < 0.05 and p_mismatch < 0.05 and |fixed sweep peak| <= 15.6 ms

tiers_not_run.mlr: impossible: the only stimulus is the authors' 100 Hz speech envelope (Nyquist 50 Hz; 30-60 Hz band beyond/at Nyquist, envelope -28 dB at 40 Hz); no audio shipped
tiers_not_run.brainstem: impossible: needs the audio waveform (half-wave rectified, 30-250 Hz); not shipped

global_offset_estimate.note: positive = levy2024 EEG fits best with the envelope delayed more than in weissbart2019 (stimtrack-aligned), i.e. audio later than the onset marker; the two datasets differ in channel count, stimulus feature (authors' 100 Hz envelope vs Hilbert envelope of the audio) and population, so the refit-sweep peak difference is an estimate, not a calibration

latency_trf_fc.method: forward TRF of the envelope, 128 Hz, 1-15 Hz, lags -200..600 ms, alpha 1, FC mean (Fz Cz F3 F4 C3 C4), avg ref (64 ch); P1 = max 20-90 ms, N1 = min 70-200 ms, P2 = max 150-300 ms; GFP over 64 ch, peak 20-400 ms
